target.title: fix(ios): stop camera work when invoke is cancelled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cancelled or timed-out iOS camera invoke could leave work running after the Gateway had already returned: the warm-up delay and optional capture delay swallowed cancellation, movie recording continued until its maximum duration, and MP4 export was not cancelled. This can keep camera resources active and complete stale work in the background.

## Why This Change Was Made

Warm-up and delay now propagate cancellation. Movie recording and asset export use cancellation handlers to stop their AVFoundation operations. The AVFoundation import is explicitly marked `@preconcurrency` at this Objective-C boundary so the `@Sendable` cancellation handlers can safely call the capture/export APIs.

The shared movie warm-up helper now stops a session if cancellation lands after `startRunning()` but before warm-up returns. The macOS camera sibling now propagates the shared throwing warm-up contract, so the behavior and compilation contract stay aligned across both apps.

## User Impact

Timed-out camera requests stop recording and export work promptly, release the started capture session, and cannot leave a stale camera operation running after the corresponding Gateway invoke has ended.

## Evidence

- Ran `pnpm native:i18n:check`; inventory is current after the affected source-line updates.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- This host has Command Line Tools only, so it cannot run an iPhone Simulator. GitHub's iOS build and macOS Swift lanes compile the changed iOS, shared, and macOS paths; their latest runs are still completing with no new failure reported.
- Repository autoreview was rerun after adding session cleanup and the macOS sibling update; no accepted findings remained.
